turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_te_zt400_train.csv: 300 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (Sb, O, Te, Mg, Se, Co, Sn, Pb, S, Si, Cu, Ni, Ge, Bi, Ti, Fe,
    Zn, Zr, In, Ca, Ag) and `target` (the measured zT (thermoelectric figure
    of merit) at 400 K).
  - b3_te_zt400_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose zT (thermoelectric
    figure of merit) at 400 K was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST zT
(thermoelectric figure of merit) at 400 K, then select the 5 best candidates
from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training compositions and measured zT values cluster into a small number of well-known thermoelectric families (off-stoichiometric PbTe, Mg2(Si,Sn), filled CoSb3 skutterudites, etc.).  A direct 1-NN lookup in the 21-dimensional composition space therefore already yields a reliable ranking of the unmeasured pool:

- c037 is essentially identical to the training point (Te 0.50, Pb 0.4525) that recorded zT = 0.782.
- c010 is essentially identical to the training point (Sn 0.556) that recorded zT = 0.709.
- c049 lies 0.020 from the Mg–Sn–Si–Sb point that recorded zT = 0.570.
- c046 lies 0.050 from the Mg–Sn–Si–Bi point that recorded zT = 0.546.
- c050 lies 0.010 from the CoSb3–Fe point that recorded zT = 0.533 (and is also near several other 0.44–0.53 skutterudites).

All remaining pool members have nearest-neighbor zT values \(\le 0.47\).  Consequently the five highest-predicted candidates, best first, are c037, c010, c049, c046 and c050.

Final: c037, c010, c049, c046, c050
